name: Spanish Squat Isometric Hold
purpose: Patellar tendon analgesia and quadriceps isometric recruitment with reduced patellofemoral joint shear.
instructions: Secure a rigid or heavy resistance band around an anchor and behind both knees immediately below the joint line.
Step back until firm forward tension is felt against the proximal shins.
Maintain a vertical shin angle and descend into roughly 70-80 degrees of knee flexion.
Hold the isometric position without allowing knees to drift forward over toes.
Breathe rhythmically throughout the hold, then smoothly rise to standing.
precautions: Keep shins as vertical as possible to minimize patellofemoral compressive reaction force.
Do not push into sharp pinching pain; terminate if discomfort exceeds 3/10.
verified_sources: Rio E, Kidgell D, Purdam C, et al. Isometric exercise induces analgesia and reduces inhibition in patellar tendinopathy. Br J Sports Med. 2015;49(19):1277-1283.
review_notes: Clinically established isometric protocol for patellar tendon load management.

name: Supine Straight Leg Raise
purpose: Quadriceps activation and anterior kinetic chain control without patellofemoral compressive contact pressure.
instructions: Lie supine on a firm surface with the unaffected knee flexed and foot flat on the floor.
Fully extend the involved knee, dorsiflex ankle, and contract quadriceps firmly.
Slowly raise the straight leg to the level of the contralateral flexed knee (approx. 45 degrees).
Pause for 2 seconds at peak elevation maintaining knee lock.
Lower under control over 2-3 seconds.
precautions: Keep lumbar spine neutral against the mat without compensatory arching.
Maintain active quadriceps lockout throughout the ascent and descent.
verified_sources: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS). Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome Rehabilitation Exercises.
review_notes: Standard non-compressive quadriceps re-education exercise from AAOS guidelines.

name: Terminal Knee Extension (TKE) with Band
purpose: Vastus medialis oblique (VMO) recruitment through terminal 0-30 degrees of knee extension.
instructions: Anchor a loop resistance band at knee height.
Step into the loop with the band positioned behind the popliteal crease.
Press the knee back into terminal extension against band resistance.
Hold peak contraction for 2 seconds, then return smoothly.
precautions: Do not forcefully snap the knee into hyperextension.
verified_sources: National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA) Corrective Exercise Review
review_notes: Awaiting dosage validation and institutional clinical review for patellofemoral sub-cohorts.

name: Wall Slide Partial Squat
purpose: Closed-chain quadriceps loading through shallow range of motion.
instructions: Stand with back flat against a wall, feet shoulder-width and 18 inches forward.
Slide down until knees reach no more than 45-60 degrees flexion.
Hold for 3 seconds, then slide back up.
precautions: Do not slide past 60 degrees during early recovery.
verified_sources: ACSM Exercise Testing and Prescription Guidelines
review_notes: Pending institutional clinical review regarding patellofemoral shear loads.

name: Prone Y-T-W Scapular Raises
purpose: Lower trapezius, middle trapezius, and serratus activation for scapular dyskinesis recovery.
instructions: Lie prone on a mat with forehead supported and neck in neutral alignment.
Y position: Raise arms at 45 degrees thumbs up; squeeze lower shoulder blades for 2 seconds.
T position: Extend arms straight out to sides, retracting mid-scapulae for 2 seconds.
W position: Flex elbows to 90 degrees, externally rotating and depressing scapulae for 2 seconds.
Lower smoothly with controlled tempo between shapes.
precautions: Avoid upper trapezius shrugging; initiate all movement from lower/mid scapular retraction.
Bodyweight only during early recovery.
verified_sources: Kibler WB, Ludewig PM, McClure PW, et al. Clinical implications of scapular dyskinesis in shoulder injury: the 2013 consensus statement. Br J Sports Med. 2013;47(14):877-885.
review_notes: Consensus-backed scapular dyskinesis rehabilitation protocol.

name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
purpose: Infraspinatus and teres minor strengthening to stabilize the humeral head against anterior migration.
instructions: Lie on the unaffected side with a folded towel roll placed between involved elbow and ribcage.
Flex involved elbow to 90 degrees.
Holding a 1-2 kg dumbbell, rotate forearm upward toward ceiling.
Pause for 1 second at apex without rolling torso backward.
Lower slowly over 3 seconds to starting horizontal position.
precautions: Keep elbow pinned firmly to the towel roll; avoid shoulder abduction.
Stop before fatigue compromises movement mechanics.
verified_sources: Reinold MM, Wilk KE, Fleisig GS, et al. Electromyographic analysis of the rotator cuff and deltoid musculature during common shoulder rehabilitation exercises. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2004;34(7):385-394.
review_notes: High EMG specificity for infraspinatus with minimal deltoid co-contraction.

name: Forearm Scapular Wall Slide
purpose: Upward scapular rotation and serratus anterior recruitment.
instructions: Stand facing a wall with forearms resting vertically against it.
Slide forearms upward along the wall into a shallow 'V' shape.
Return slowly to start.
precautions: Cease upward slide prior to anterior pinching.
verified_sources: Cools AM, et al. Scapular muscle recruitment during rehabilitation exercises. Am J Sports Med. 2007.
review_notes: Requires impingement sub-cohort clearance before automated recommendation.

name: Gentle Sleeper Posterior Capsule Stretch
purpose: Posterior capsule mobilization for internal rotation deficit in overhead athletes.
instructions: Lie on involved side with shoulder and elbow flexed to 90 degrees.
Use opposite hand to gently push wrist down toward the mat into internal rotation.
Hold for 30 seconds.
precautions: Apply gentle pressure only; avoid anterior joint pinching.
verified_sources: Wilk KE, et al. The athlete's shoulder rehabilitation. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2012.
review_notes: Pending clinical consensus regarding subacromial contact pressures in acute pain.

name: Quadruped Bird-Dog
purpose: Spinal stabilization, multifidus activation, and anti-rotational core endurance with minimal compressive axial load.
instructions: Begin on all fours on a padded mat with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace core gently while maintaining neutral lumbar lordosis.
Slowly extend right arm forward and left leg backward until both align horizontally with torso.
Hold isometric position for 4 seconds without pelvic rotation or lumbar hyperextension.
Return to quadruped and alternate opposite extremities.
precautions: Do not raise limbs above horizontal level; avoid hyperextending lumbar spine.
Maintain neutral cervical spine looking downward.
verified_sources: McGill SM. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation. Human Kinetics; 2007.
review_notes: Extensively documented low-load spine stabilization exercise (McGill 'Big 3').

name: McGill Modified Curl-Up
purpose: Anterior core activation with zero lumbar flexion shear or disc protrusion pressure.
instructions: Lie supine with one leg straight and one knee bent with foot on the floor.
Place palms facing downward under the lumbar spine to preserve natural lordotic curve.
Elevate head and shoulder blades slightly off the floor (clearing floor by 1-2 inches).
Hold isometric contraction for 7-8 seconds while breathing continuously.
Lower head smoothly, resting 2 seconds before the next repetition.
precautions: Do not tuck chin or curl the lumbar spine; motion originates strictly at thoracic level.
Hands must remain under lower back to verify lordosis maintenance.
verified_sources: McGill SM. Low Back Exercises: Evidence for Improving Exercise Regimens. Phys Ther. 1998;78(7):754-765.
review_notes: Clinical gold standard for anterior abdominal endurance without lumbar flexion strain.

name: Gentle Cat-Cow Segmental Mobilization
purpose: Segmental spinal mobility within comfortable mid-range tolerance.
instructions: Start on all fours with wrists under shoulders.
Inhale, softly dipping the belly while elevating the chest.
Exhale, gently rounding the spine toward the ceiling.
Move smoothly through pain-free range.
precautions: Avoid pushing into painful end-ranges.
verified_sources: Mayo Clinic Back Conditioning Exercises
review_notes: Pending clinical panel dosage review for acute disc herniation sub-cohorts.

name: Supine Glute Bridge Isometric Hold
purpose: Gluteus maximus activation and pelvic stability to offload compensatory lumbar erector dominance.
instructions: Lie supine with knees bent to 90 degrees, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Engage core brace and drive through heels to elevate hips until thighs align with torso.
Squeeze glutes at the top without hyperextending lumbar spine.
Hold isometric position for 5 seconds, breathing rhythmically.
Lower hips under control.
precautions: Do not arch lumbar spine to gain artificial elevation; lift through hip extension.
Distribute weight evenly through heels.
verified_sources: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS). Spine Conditioning Program.
review_notes: Standard pelvic stabilization drill from AAOS Spine Rehabilitation guidelines.

name: Supine Submaximal Hamstring Bridge on Bench
purpose: Tendon remodeling and isometric bicep femoris recruitment at lengthened position.
instructions: Lie supine with heels resting on a low bench, knees flexed to 45 degrees.
Drive heels down into bench to elevate hips 2 inches.
Hold isometric hold for 30 seconds.
precautions: Use double leg hold initially; no ballistic loading.
verified_sources: Macdonald B, et al. Hamstring strain injury rehabilitation. Sports Med. 2019.
review_notes: Pending clinical protocol validation regarding proximal tendon compression.

name: Assisted Eccentric Hamstring Slider
purpose: Submaximal eccentric loading to build strain resistance.
instructions: Lie on back with sliders under heels.
Bridge hips up and slowly slide heels away over 4 seconds.
Lower hips to floor before resetting.
precautions: Double leg only; no active concentric curl under heavy load.
verified_sources: Askling CM, et al. Hamstring eccentric loading protocols. Br J Sports Med. 2013.
review_notes: Requires physical therapy oversight during eccentric phase.

name: Tibialis Anterior Wall Raises
purpose: Anterior compartment endurance and deceleration force absorption for shin splint recovery.
instructions: Lean against wall with feet 12 inches out.
Pull toes and forefoot up toward shins.
Hold for 1 second, then lower.
precautions: Do not rock hips forward.
verified_sources: Moen MH, et al. Medial tibial stress syndrome management. Sports Med. 2009.
review_notes: Pending clinical validation for tibial stress fracture differentiation.

name: Seated Bent-Knee Soleus Heel Raises
purpose: Heavy slow resistance load for soleus and Achilles tendon with decreased gastrocnemius contribution.
instructions: Sit upright in a chair with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor.
Drive through balls of feet to elevate heels into maximal plantarflexion.
Pause for 2 seconds at peak contraction.
Lower heels slowly over 3 seconds to a full comfortable stretch.
precautions: Execute with slow controlled cadence; avoid bouncing through end-range.
Discontinue if sharp localized retrocalcaneal pain occurs.
verified_sources: Beyer R, Kongsgaard M, Hougs Kjær B, et al. Heavy Slow Resistance Versus Eccentric Training for Achilles Tendinopathy: A Randomized Controlled Trial. Am J Sports Med. 2015;43(7):1704-1711.
review_notes: Clinically proven Heavy Slow Resistance protocol for Achilles/soleus tendon remodeling.

name: Ankle Multi-Planar Alphabet Mobilization
purpose: Restoration of multi-planar range of motion and neuromuscular proprioception post-inversion sprain.
instructions: Sit with involved lower extremity elevated and foot freely suspended in air.
Using the hallux (big toe) as a pointer, trace capital letters of the alphabet from A to Z.
Form broad, deliberate movements through pain-free range of motion without rotating tibia.
precautions: Execute strictly within pain-free boundaries.
Keep lower leg stable; motion must come from talocrural and subtalar joints.
verified_sources: Kaminski TW, Hertel J, Amendola N, et al. National Athletic Trainers' Association Position Statement: Conservative Management and Prevention of Ankle Sprains in Athletes. J Athl Train. 2013;48(4):528-545.
review_notes: NATA position statement recommended early mobilization for lateral ankle sprains.

name: Cervical Retraction (Chin Tucks)
purpose: Deep cervical flexor (longus colli/capitis) activation and suboccipital decompression.
instructions: Sit or stand upright with shoulders relaxed and gaze horizontal.
Draw the chin horizontally straight back (creating a subtle double chin) without flexing or extending the neck.
Hold the retracted position for 5 seconds feeling a gentle elongation at base of skull.
Release smoothly to neutral with relaxed breathing.
precautions: Do not tilt head downward; keep motion in a purely horizontal anterior-posterior plane.
Stop immediately if any dizziness, lightheadedness, or visual changes occur.
verified_sources: Jull G, Falla D, Treleaven J, et al. Retraining cervical flexor muscle performance in chronic neck pain. Spine. 2008.
review_notes: Clinical trial evidence for deep neck flexor stabilization in cervical dysfunction.

name: Thoracic Extension over Foam Roller
purpose: Thoracic extension mobility restoration to relieve cervical compensatory stress.
instructions: Position foam roller horizontally beneath upper thoracic spine.
Support head with hands and gently extend upper back.
Hold 3-5 seconds, then return.
precautions: Support head at all times; do not roll onto lumbar spine.
verified_sources: APTA Orthopaedic Section Thoracic Guidelines
review_notes: Pending clinical review for thoracic kyphosis and osteopenia safety margins.

name: Side-Lying Clamshell
purpose: Gluteus medius activation to control femoral internal rotation.
instructions: Lie on unaffected side with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet touching.
Raise top knee while keeping heels together.
Hold 2 seconds, then lower.
precautions: Do not roll pelvis backward.
verified_sources: Distefano LJ, et al. Gluteal muscle activation during rehabilitation. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2009.
review_notes: Pending clinical panel dosage review for tensor fasciae latae dominance screening.
